subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current docs and tests intentionally preserve session-level `/exec` defaults, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because later operator policy changes can be shadowed by old session state.

options.title: Make config the safety ceiling
options.body: Clamp or clear persisted session exec fields that are less restrictive than current global or agent policy, with upgrade/reset coverage for existing entries.

options.title: Keep session persistence as-is
options.body: Document that operators must reset or repair sessions to enforce changed exec policy for existing Discord lanes.

options.title: Add explicit reset or doctor repair first
options.body: Ship an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Make config the safety ceiling
recommendation.body: Clamp or clear persisted session exec fields that are less restrictive than current global or agent policy, with upgrade/reset coverage for existing entries.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for `/exec` session overrides and resolver tests points to this account/name path.
